newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says Moscow's line on NATO unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Moscow's line on NATO unchanged.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, meeting top Kremlin officials on Friday, days before a European security summit, took a tough line over NATO's plans to expand eastwards.

"Russia's stance on NATO expansion remains unchanged, that is, negative," spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky quoted Yeltsin as saying in a meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.

"Even if some want it or not, NATO expansion will lead to new divisions in Europe," Yeltsin said. His statement was the latest in a series of harsh statements from Moscow in recent days on the NATO issue.

Chernomyrdin will lead the Russian delegation to the Lisbon summit of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) next week. Yeltsin, recovering from heart surgery, will remain in Moscow.
Russia wants to persuade its sceptical Western partners that the OSCE should have a leading role in security matters in Europe and act as a counterbalance to NATO.
Yeltsin said he wanted the summit to aim for "a new architecture of European security.
